narrative.executive_summary: The search looked for new sodium solid electrolytes from Na3PS4 or Na3SbS4 that resist sodium metal and conduct Na+. The champion is Na3PSeS3 from parent Na3PS4 with space group Cc. Its energy above hull is 0.002 eV/atom with an error bar of 0.002 eV/atom, its band gaps are 2.266 eV and 2.931 eV, and its electrochemical window is from 1.52 V to 1.7 V with passivating behavior against sodium metal. Its diffusion coefficient at 600 K is 2.16e-07 cm²/s with an error of 1.42e-07 cm²/s and a verdict of tied against its parent, which means no difference was shown and not equal conduction. Ionic conductivity at 300 K was not computed. The other finalists are Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and Na6P2SeS7, for which diffusion was not simulated. The champion composition is already published as part of Na3PS4-xSex. The candidates are computational predictions, not proven materials.

review.headline: The campaign's champion computational prediction is Na3PSeS3, which passed stability, band gap and sodium-metal passivation tests but only tied its parent in diffusion at 600 K.
learned: After Na5PWS8 failed sodium-metal contact, later rounds avoided reducible tungsten and shifted toward isovalent selenium, antimony and germanium substitutions, whereas halogen-plus-vacancy and antimony-selenium proposals still failed their fixed tests.

Selenium for sulfur in Na3PS4 held across doses: Na3PSeS3 had an energy above the hull of 0.002 eV/atom and a band gap of 2.27 eV, while Na6P2SeS7 had an energy above the hull of 0.002 eV/atom and a band gap of 2.26 eV.
The same selenium idea did not hold on the antimony sulfide parent, as Na3SbSeS3 had a band gap of 1.77 eV and was rejected.

Germanium for silicon in the NASICON parent also held from Na3Zr2SiGePO12, with an energy above the hull of 0.002 eV/atom and a band gap of 4.20 eV, to fully substituted Na3Zr2Ge2PO12, with an energy above the hull of 0.003 eV/atom and a band gap of 3.98 eV.
Antimony for phosphorus in Na6SbPS8 passed with a band gap of 2.24 eV and passivating behaviour, but its energy above the hull of 0.008 eV/atom was higher than the selenium-for-sulfur candidates.
worked: Na3PSeS3 ranked first among the finalists because its energy above the hull per substitution was 0.018 eV, below 0.026 eV for Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and 0.031 eV for Na6P2SeS7, and it was passivating against sodium metal with a band gap of 2.27 eV.

Na3PSeS3 was the only finalist with simulated diffusion, giving a diffusion coefficient of 2.16e-07 cm²/s at 600 K and diffusion against the parent of 0.94 ± 0.71, which the fixed rules recorded as tied.
Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and Na6P2SeS7 passed as finalists with passivating behaviour and band gaps of 3.98 eV and 2.26 eV respectively, although diffusion was not simulated for either compound.
failed: Na5PWS8 failed contact with sodium metal as non-passivating with a reaction energy of 1.452 eV/atom, possibly because reducible tungsten may have formed metallic tungsten.
Na3SbSeS3 was rejected for a band gap of 1.77 eV, below the 1.8 eV threshold, possibly because the antimony-selenium combination may have lowered the band gap more than phosphorus-selenium.

Na5P2S7Br was rejected for an energy above the hull of 0.061 eV/atom, above the 0.05 eV/atom threshold, possibly because bromine substitution combined with a sodium vacancy may have destabilised the sulfide framework.

Na3HfZrSi2PO12 was rejected because its composition was already known, possibly because hafnium-for-zirconium expansion may have reproduced an existing NASICON composition rather than a distinct prediction.

next_campaign.goal: Find sodium solid electrolyte computational predictions from Na3PS4, Na3SbS4 or Na3Zr2Si2PO12 that improve diffusion against their parent while staying passivating against sodium metal.
directions: Test minimal co-doping in Na3PS4 with one to two selenium substitutions plus one antimony substitution, without sodium vacancies.
Test single-site tellurium for sulfur in Na3PS4 without sodium vacancies, checking energy above the hull and band gap against the fixed thresholds.
Run diffusion simulations at 600 K for the already passing Na6P2SeS7, Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and Na6SbPS8 before proposing further analogues.
next_campaign.why: Selenium and germanium expansions passed with energies above the hull near 0.002 eV/atom and band gaps above 2.26 eV, but the only simulated diffusion result was tied with its parent. The next campaign should therefore test whether small co-doping changes diffusion while avoiding the tungsten, bromine-vacancy and antimony-selenium failures seen here.

summaries.text: In iteration 1 the agent tested sulfide/ selenide substitutions and isovalent NASICON expansion for sodium solid electrolytes to keep stability against sodium metal and widen sodium migration pathways. Na3PSeS3 and Na3Zr2SiGePO12 were predicted stable with energy above the hull near 0.00 eV per atom and band gaps of about 2.3 eV and 4.2 eV respectively, and Na3PSeS3 showed sodium diffusion at 600 K tied with its parent. Na5PWS8 was predicted stable with energy above the hull about 0.02 eV per atom and a band gap of about 2.1 eV but failed contact with sodium metal because tungsten is reduced to metallic tungsten with a driving force of about 1.45 eV per atom. The agent concluded that S to Se anion mixing and isovalent Si to Ge NASICON expansion can retain passivation, while aliovalent tungsten for phosphorus introduces reducible d-metal reduction, and will next explore S to Se/Te mixing and isovalent NASICON expansion avoiding reducible cations.
summaries.label: iteration 1

summaries.text: In iteration 2 the agent tested isovalent soft-anion expansion with Se, Sb, Ge and a halogen induced sodium vacancy to widen Na+ pathways while keeping sodium metal passivation and avoiding reducible tungsten. Na3SbSeS3 was rejected at the band gap filter with a gap of about 1.8 eV, below the 1.8 eV target, and Na5P2S7Br was rejected at the hull filter with energy above the hull of about 0.06 eV per atom above the 0.05 eV per atom limit. Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 passed both filters with energy above the hull near 0.00 eV per atom and a band gap of about 4.0 eV, suggesting the fully substituted NASICON germanium expansion remains passivating and more stable per substitution than earlier variants.
summaries.label: iteration 2

summaries.text: In this iteration the agent tried isovalent soft-anion and pnictogen substitutions in Na3PS4 and Hf-expanded NASICON to widen Na+ pathways while keeping passivation and gaps. Na6P2SeS7 and Na6SbPS8 passed with low energy above the hull of about 0.00 eV per atom and 0.01 eV per atom and band gaps of about 2.3 eV and 2.2 eV, while Na3HfZrSi2PO12 was rejected because the composition is already known. The agent concluded that low-dose sulfur to selenium substitution improves stability and gap relative to other substitutions and that minimal co-doping with selenium and antimony should be tested next.
summaries.label: iteration 3

summaries.text: The agent proposed nine new sodium solid-electrolyte candidates derived from Na3PS4 or Na3SbS4 and six passed the stability and electronic filtering. Na3PSeS3 was predicted with an energy above the hull of about 0.00 eV per atom and a band gap of about 2.3 eV, and molecular dynamics found its sodium diffusion tied with the parent, about 0.94 times the parent rate. Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 was predicted with an energy above the hull of about 0.00 eV per atom and a band gap of about 4.0 eV, and Na6P2SeS7 was predicted with an energy above the hull of about 0.00 eV per atom and a band gap of about 2.3 eV. One early candidate was excluded because it was not passivating against sodium metal with metallic products and a reaction energy of 1.45 eV per atom. The run ended with three low-energy, insulating finalists, one of which shows diffusion comparable to its parent.
summaries.label: run
